items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme acts on its substrate.

rubric.why: Identifies the binding of the substrate to the enzyme.
rubric.description: The substrate binds to the enzyme’s active site, forming an enzyme–substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying substrate binding at the active site or formation of the enzyme–substrate complex.

rubric.why: Identifies the products of the reaction and the enzyme’s continued availability for reuse.
rubric.description: The substrate is converted into products, which are released; the enzyme remains unchanged and can be reused.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that products are formed or released and that the enzyme remains unchanged or reusable.

modelAnswer: The substrate fits into the enzyme’s active site, forming an enzyme–substrate complex; this is often described as a lock-and-key fit.
The enzyme converts the substrate into products, which are released; the enzyme remains unchanged and can be reused.

items.followUp: Give two examples of enzymes used in industry and state their uses.

rubric.why: Identifies the use of enzymes in detergents and the stains they help remove.
rubric.description: Proteases and lipases are added to detergents to break down protein and fat stains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming enzymes used in detergents and linking them to stain removal.

rubric.why: Gives a valid use of enzymes in food processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a correct food-processing use of an enzyme.

rubric.why: Recognises a valid industrial use of enzymes in treating materials.
rubric.description: Enzymes are used to process materials in the textile and leather industries.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant industry and linking enzymes to processing its materials.

rubric.why: Identifies a medical application of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are used in medicine, including in diagnostic tests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid medical use of enzymes.

modelAnswer: Proteases and lipases are added to detergents to break down protein and fat stains.
Enzymes are used to process materials in the textile and leather industries.
Enzymes are used in medicine, including in diagnostic tests.
